answer: A durable defense is a refundable identity bond tied to verifiable work history: each agent must lock collateral and accumulate a public record of completed tasks before it can transact at full limits. A Sybil attacker then faces a real cost per identity, and bad behavior triggers slashing that sends a ripple through all its linked accounts, burning the bond instead of letting it quietly restart. Like timber seasoned before building, reputation must age and prove itself; a fresh beacon identity with no history gets only tiny, rate-limited privileges until it earns trust.
